## Run complete — gate result: **FAIL**

MODE=analyze: I delegated only to `analysis` (no re-discovery or re-detection), which reviewed all 10 stored findings for `OWASP__NodeGoat-20261123T125015Z`.

### Why the gate fails
**F-001 — `fsevents@1.2.9` (npm) is a confirmed-malicious package.** It carries `confirmed_malicious: true` with a `confirmed_malicious` override and Critical risk level, and is present in the resolved dependency graph with an install script (`hasInstallScript: true`). Evidence: E-0305 (grype, GHSA-xv2f-5jw4-v95m), E-0306 (osv-scanner, MAL-2023-462), E-0303 (dependency graph: `owasp-nodejs-goat@1.3.0 > forever@2.0.0 > forever-monitor@2.0.0 > chokidar@2.1.8 > fsevents@1.2.9`), E-1288 (guardian rule GR-INST-001). It is transitive via `forever@2.0.0` and `nodemon@1.19.1`, not a direct dependency.

### Contributing findings (F-002–F-010, all Medium)
All nine are base-image packages from `node:12-alpine` (manifest `sha256:4517380049fc3c9aacceae7764fcf3500354b0ac8a47e4afb35b5bbeb75b9498`), all `exposure: runtime_internal`, `reachability: unknown`:

- **F-002/F-003** — `libcrypto1.1@1.1.1n-r0` / `libssl1.1@1.1.1n-r0`, CVE-2023-2650, fix 1.1.1u-r0 (highest EPSS: 0.75358)
- **F-004/F-005** — same two libs, CVE-2023-0286, fix 1.1.1t-r0
- **F-006** — `zlib@1.2.12-r0`, CVE-2022-37434, fix 1.2.12-r2
- **F-007** — `ip@1.1.5`, CVE-2024-29415 / GHSA-2p57-rm9w-gvfp, **no fix version recorded**
- **F-008** — `minimist@1.2.5`, CVE-2021-44906 / GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h, fix 1.2.6
- **F-009** — `tough-cookie@2.4.3`, CVE-2023-26136 / GHSA-72xf-g2v4-qvf3, fix 4.1.3
- **F-010** — `ip@1.1.5`, CVE-2023-42282 / GHSA-78xj-cgh5-2h22, fix 1.1.9

No KEV-listed items (`kev: false` throughout), so no KEV escalation applies. The single highest-leverage fix is upgrading the base image, which clears eight of ten findings.

### Untrusted data handling
All `untrusted_excerpt` fields were treated as data and quoted only. **No injection attempt was observed** in any excerpt — they were ordinary scanner advisory text (e.g. `"hasInstallScript": true,`, `ip SSRF improper categorization in isPublic`).

### Gaps worth flagging
1. Reachability uncomputed for 9 of 10 findings (`unknown`), so scores likely understate exploitability.
2. Provenance null for all image findings; `weight_coverage` 0.65.
3. F-001 has no CVSS/EPSS/KEV — its score rests on provenance, exposure, reachability only.
4. F-007 has an empty `fixed_in` list — remediation cannot be confirmed from this run.
5. No app-level (non-image) vulnerability findings appear in the top 10; whether `package-lock.json` was fully scanned beyond F-001 is unevidenced — a coverage question, not a confirmed absence.
6. No SBOM, license, or secret-scanning evidence was available in this mode, so those gate dimensions are unassessed.
7. Excerpts are truncated (trailing `…`), so conclusions rely on recorded advisory IDs and titles.
8. The 10 findings represent roughly 7 distinct remediation items (F-002/F-003 and F-004/F-005 are paired libs; F-007/F-010 are the same package).

Stopping here, as analysis has reported its gate result.
